newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-BOLIVIA STROLL TO WIN OVER PERU.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BOLIVIA STROLL TO WIN OVER PERU.

text.p: Hosts Bolivia strolled to a 2-0 win over a disinterested Peru in front of another disappointing crowd at the Copa America soccer tournament on Sunday.
Goals by Marco Etcheverry and Julio Baldivieso, who play in the United States and Japan respectively, gave the hosts an easy three points in Group B to ensure them of a quarter-final berth.

Peru have rested nearly all their regular internationals for World Cup qualifiers and their team was virtually an under-23 squad. But, with three points from Thursday's win over Uruguay, they could still make the last eight.
Playing at 3,600 metres above sea level, Peru was at a disadvantage from the start and did themselves no favours when Juan Reyna was sent off for an awful two-footed tackle in the 15th minute.
Etcheverry capped 45 minutes of Bolivian dominance by scoring from an unmarked position on the stroke of halftime.
Baldivieso broke through the defence and rounded Miranda to score the second five minutes after the break.
Peru seemed interested only in keeping the score down and barely ventured out of their half.
Only 10,000 fans watched Bolivia's 1-0 win over Venezuela Thursday and the 45,000 capacity Hernando Silas stadium was barely half full Sunday.

High ticket prcies and general apathy towards the tournament, crammed between crucial World Cup qualifying matches, plus an ongoing feud between the home team and local media were being blamed for the poor turnout.
